entities.name: Ali ibn Abi Bakr al-Harawi
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
ʿAlī ibn Abī Bakr al-Harawī (Abū al-Ḥasan, 'Ali of Herat'; d. 1215) was a Persian traveller, ascetic, and guidebook author of the late Ayyubid age, best known for Kitāb al-ishārāt ilā maʿrifat al-ziyārāt—a pioneering manual of pilgrimage sites across Syria, Palestine, Egypt, and beyond. Writing for devout visitors, he catalogued tombs of prophets, Companions, and saints, blending topography, miracle lore, and practical itinerary.

Al-Harawī's career unfolded amid Crusader–Muslim contest for the Levant: sacred geography was political as well as pious. His notices preserve otherwise lost local traditions about shrines, city gates, and battle memories, making him indispensable for historians of Islamic sacred space and for archaeologists tracing medieval ziyāra circuits.

Unlike purely literary geographers, he wrote as a peripatetic devotee who claimed personal inspection. The Ishārāt thus stands at the junction of travel narrative, hagiology, and urban topography—an early specialised pilgrimage guide that shaped later Levantine shrine literature.
